o: We have a table of per-minute order counts and must bundle minutes into consecutive blocks of 6 (minutes 1–6 = interval 1, 7–12 = interval 2, …), summing `order_count` per block. In Example 1, minutes 1–6 sum to 17 and minutes 7–12 sum to 18. Since `minute` starts at 1 and rows are guaranteed to tile complete intervals, a simple integer mapping `interval_no = CEIL(minute / 6)` (equivalently `FLOOR((minute-1)/6)+1`) turns this into a plain GROUP BY aggregate. Constraints are tiny, so any grouping expression works.
k: Interval number is just CEIL(minute/6) — no window functions needed.
GROUP BY can reference the computed alias in MySQL.

a.i: Map each minute to its interval index with ceiling division, then aggregate. Because minute/6 on integers yields a decimal in MySQL, CEIL behaves correctly.

c.python:
-- MySQL
SELECT CEIL(minute / 6) AS interval_no,
       SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY interval_no
ORDER BY interval_no;
c.cpp:
-- PostgreSQL
SELECT CEILING(minute / 6.0)::int AS interval_no,
       SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
c.java:
-- Oracle
SELECT CEIL(minute / 6) AS interval_no,
       SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CEIL(minute / 6)
ORDER BY interval_no;
c.javascript:
-- SQLite
SELECT CAST((minute + 5) / 6 AS INTEGER) AS interval_no,
       SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY interval_no
ORDER BY interval_no;

a.t: O(R log R) for grouping/sorting R rows (R is small)

a.i: Same idea using FLOOR((minute-1)/6)+1, which avoids decimal division and works uniformly across engines.
s: Shift minute by -1 so each interval starts at a multiple of 6

c.python:
-- MySQL
SELECT FLOOR((minute - 1) / 6) + 1 AS interval_no,
       SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY interval_no
ORDER BY interval_no;
c.cpp:
-- PostgreSQL
SELECT (minute - 1) / 6 + 1 AS interval_no,
       SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
c.java:
-- Oracle
SELECT FLOOR((minute - 1) / 6) + 1 AS interval_no,
       SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY FLOOR((minute - 1) / 6)
ORDER BY 1;
c.javascript:
-- SQLite
SELECT (minute - 1) / 6 + 1 AS interval_no,
       SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY interval_no
ORDER BY interval_no;

w: Either query is fine in an interview; prefer CEIL(minute/6) for readability. Pitfall: in engines with integer division (PostgreSQL, SQLite), dividing integers by 6 truncates — shift by 1 or cast to decimal first. Follow-up: what if intervals were 60 minutes, or the table had gaps? The same expression still works.
